replaces: Freeze-1.1 §3 para 1 and §8.2 discovery index (public Bing web-search result HTML), and the Freeze-1.2 rev-1 Bing runner
reason: External review found material uncertainty over whether automated retrieval, parsing and archival of Bing search-result HTML is permitted under Microsoft's public terms. Technical accessibility is not permission. Withdrawn before any Bing or other discovery request.

design_inputs_examined.note: No discovery endpoint was queried. No catalog, repository or vendor listing was opened.

evaluated_classes.basis: terms uncertainty (external review); not permitted merely because accessible
require account creation and an API credential, which this protocol stage forbids; retention/publication rights would need a paid plan. Their terms were not relied on and no request was made.
zenodo.org/robots.txt: 'User-agent: * Disallow: /search Disallow: /api'. The policy/robots basis for automated search is ambiguous, even though its metadata is CC0.

Policy permits harvesting ('All metadata is exported via OAI-PMH and can be harvested', CC0), but discovery would need a full-repository harvest (millions of records at 30 req/min) plus an untested local query semantics. Recorded as a possible future preregistered addition; not a silent substitute.
a single maintainer cannot meet >=2 independently controlled maintainers; enumerating by chosen ontology classes/properties is discretionary
they enumerate packages, not vendor platforms; restricting to SDK-publishing vendors would change the target population

evaluated_classes.class: named public API catalogues chosen by the researchers
evaluated_classes.basis: choosing named catalogs from researcher memory reintroduces the discretionary source choice that Freeze 1.1 repaired

rule.discovery_index: GitHub REST API, GET https://api.github.com/search/repositories, unauthenticated, no account, no credential
queries: open software API catalog CSV JSON
public developer platform registry bulk export
rule.query_construction: q = '<frozen Freeze-1.1 query verbatim> in:name,description,topics,readme'; per_page=20; page=1; no sort parameter (API default best match); no other qualifiers
rule.query_rationale: Same four Freeze-1.1 query strings, not tuned. 'in:...readme' is added because the default searches only name/description/topics, and a README is the repository's landing text (the analogue of the page a web engine indexes). Not tested against live results.
rule.positions: items 1..min(20,total_count) of each response, in response order
rule.complete_response: incomplete_results=false and item count == min(20,total_count); total_count below 20 is a complete (short) result, not a failure
rule.union: discovered-source set = union over the four queries, keyed by repository id; every (query, position) occurrence recorded; forks and mirrors resolved to canonical upstream during screening (Freeze 1.1 §3)
rule.screening: Freeze-1.1 §3/§8.2 source checklist unchanged, applied in normalized html_url byte order by the two registered adjudicators, plus S-LIC and S-ACCESS below

additional_source_criteria.S-LIC: The enumeration's repository or distribution carries an explicit licence or public-domain dedication permitting reproduction and redistribution for research (OSI-approved software licence, CC0, CC BY, CC BY-SA, ODbL/ODC-By, or explicit public-domain statement). TRUE if one is present in the repository root LICENSE*/COPYING*, README or data-file metadata at the T0 version; FALSE if none of these contains any licence statement; UNRESOLVED if the licence is non-standard, non-commercial, no-derivatives, contradictory or unreadable.
additional_source_criteria.S-ACCESS: The complete enumeration version <=T0 is retrievable by a permitted automated mechanism: TRUE if it is an immutable data file in the public GitHub repository (git over HTTPS or the GitHub REST API); for an off-GitHub official distribution, TRUE only with an explicit licence/terms grant covering automated retrieval, FALSE if its robots.txt disallows the path or its terms prohibit automated access, otherwise UNRESOLVED.
additional_source_criteria.precedence: Freeze-1.1 precedence applies: any affirmative FALSE => SOURCE_INELIGIBLE; all TRUE => SOURCE_ELIGIBLE; otherwise SOURCE_UNRESOLVED, which blocks source lock

rule.minimum_sources: all qualifying upstream enumerations, with >=2 independently controlled maintainers (Freeze 1.1, unchanged); fewer halts the frame; no substitute catalog

github_aup_section_7_verbatim: You may use information from our Service for the following reasons, regardless of whether the information was scraped, collected through our API, or obtained otherwise:
Researchers may use public, non-personal information from the Service for research purposes, only if any publications resulting from that research are open access.
Scraping does not refer to the collection of information through our API. Please see Section H of our Terms of Service for our API Terms.
Your use of information from the Service must comply with the GitHub Privacy Statement.
github_tos_section_h_verbatim: Abuse or excessively frequent requests to GitHub via the API may result in the temporary or permanent suspension of your Account's access to the API.

You may not use the API to download data or Content from GitHub for spamming purposes, including for the purposes of selling GitHub users' personal information, such as to recruiters, headhunters, and job boards.
automated_access_basis.rate_limit_doc: unauthenticated search: up to 10 requests per minute; this protocol makes 4 search requests 60 s apart
automated_access_basis.robots: https://api.github.com/robots.txt returned HTTP 404 on 2026-09-18 (RFC 9309: no restriction); re-checked at preflight
binding_conditions: every resulting Programme A publication is open access (condition of the research clause)
only public, non-personal information is published: owner logins, avatars and user objects are excluded from published projections
no spamming or sale of personal information

capture_representation.raw: exact response bytes written O_EXCL to a custody directory outside the repository (~/.firstcall-custody/programme-a/authoritative-2026-09-23T0900Z); never published because responses contain user objects (personal information); disclosed to auditors on request under the same research terms
capture_representation.published: per response: request URL, status, selected headers (date, x-github-request-id, rate-limit headers, content-type), timing, raw SHA256, raw byte count, and a deterministic canonical projection: total_count, incomplete_results, and per item position, id, full_name, html_url, owner_type, fork, archived, created_at, pushed_at, default_branch, license_spdx_id
capture_representation.auditability: The projection function is in the digested runner, so anyone holding the raw bytes can reproduce the projection and both hashes. Repository ids plus commit SHAs <=T0 make the source universe itself immutable and publicly re-retrievable. Nothing about auditability is weakened silently: raw bytes are withheld from publication only because of personal-information restrictions.
capture_representation.residual: full_name (owner/repo) contains the owner login for user-owned repositories; it is published as the repository's public address because provenance needs it

failure_policy.terms_changed: preflight fetches the GitHub AUP page and requires the registered sentences (after tag stripping and whitespace normalisation); any missing => TERMS_CHANGED halt before any search request
failure_policy.robots_disallows: ROBOTS_DISALLOW halt; 5xx/unreachable => ROBOTS_UNVERIFIED halt (RFC 9309); 4xx => no restriction
failure_policy.source_unavailable: network error, timeout, non-200 or redirect => halt; no retry; later queries not issued
failure_policy.malformed_response: non-JSON, missing fields, or item count != min(20,total_count) => MALFORMED_RESPONSE halt after custody write
failure_policy.duplicate_enumeration: same repository id across queries => one discovered source with all occurrences recorded; mirrors/forks resolved by upstream identity at screening; never extra sampling weight
failure_policy.source_changed_after_capture: the source version is the latest commit <=T0; a force-push or rewrite that removes it => source-lock STOP (Freeze 1.1), unless a byte-identical copy verified against the recorded commit/tree hash is available
failure_policy.source_disappears_between_capture_and_lo: deleted/renamed/private repository => SOURCE_UNRESOLVED => blocks lock; no substitute
failure_policy.terms_change_after_capture: a later change never retroactively licenses or unlicenses the capture; S-LIC is judged at the T0 version; a new prohibition before retrieval of a source's content => that source UNRESOLVED
failure_policy.all_failures: any capture halt is final for this cohort; no alternate session; a new cohort needs a new prospective amendment

coverage_and_estimand.estimand_text: unchanged: Freeze-1.1 §8.6 P_v over canonical platforms in the sealed source-union frame ... under the frozen natural customer run condition
coverage_and_estimand.declared_support_change: The discoverable-source class narrows from 'enumerations reachable through the top-20 English/GB Bing web results for four queries' to 'public GitHub repositories matching the same four queries in name/description/topics/README (top 20 each)', with explicit reuse licences (S-LIC) and a permitted automated retrieval path (S-ACCESS). Qualifying enumerations hosted only off GitHub are no longer discoverable. Vendor-level inclusion, identity, strata, eligibility, prior-target exclusion and UK-customer context are unchanged.
coverage_and_estimand.materiality_assessment: The estimand is frame-relative by construction (Freeze 1.1 §3: 'Membership in a catalog is a coverage mechanism, not a random sample of all software. Outside-union probabilities are unknown'). The realized frame under either index was unknown in advance and neither was ever observed, so no vendor population is being traded for another on outcome grounds. The change is therefore declared as a support change of the discovery layer, not an estimand change. It is not hidden: every report must state the GitHub-hosted, licensed-catalog support. The researcher must accept it at anchoring; if it is judged material, the correct response is NOT to anchor.
coverage_and_estimand.unknowns: The overlap between Bing-discoverable and GitHub-discoverable qualifying catalogs is unknown and is not estimated from memory. Whether >=2 independent qualifying maintainers will be found is untested; failure halts.

biases_disclosed: GitHub best-match ranking (signals undocumented, may include popularity) with top-20 truncation; total_count published
